intro.caption: Lesson 3-7 — converting measurements between systems. Drift League's International Cup brings tracks from around the world, so crews must convert between customary and metric units.

balloons.t: Welcome to Cup Quiz! Tonight's winner takes pole position—and I already ate the catering!
Different systems on every card. Estimate unit size first, then convert!
5 kilometers and 5 miles both say 5! So they're the exact same race!
Yeah, and 5 pennies equals 5 dollars! Check the unit size first!

pages.caption: Same number, different units means different amounts. One mile is longer than one kilometer.

balloons.t: Before we multiply, which unit is bigger? And is the factor exact or rounded?
Write the conversion factor as a ratio, then scale both columns by the same number.
Watch the decimal point when you scale by 10 or 50!
The Vipers just divided when they should have multiplied! Can Drift Crew catch it?
Always check: smaller unit gets a BIGGER number, larger unit gets a SMALLER number.
Three championship questions across systems. Let's lock in pole position!
Drift Crew sweeps the International Cup Quiz! Pole position is theirs!

win.caption: Converting between customary and metric systems uses a conversion factor and ratio scaling. Use ≈ for rounded factors and always check unit-size direction.

gates.title: Gate 1 · Estimate First
gates.prompt: Round 1 asks you to compare units and symbols before you calculate.
hints: Conceptual: a mile is longer than a kilometer (1 km ≈ 0.6 mi), so 5 miles covers more ground than 5 km.
Procedural: use = only when a conversion factor is exact by definition (1 in = 2.54 cm); use ≈ when it is rounded.

steps: Practice: compare 10 inches and 10 centimeters (1 in = 2.54 cm).
One inch is more than 2 centimeters long, so 10 inches is longer than 10 centimeters.
worked.q: Which is heavier: 4 pounds or 4 kilograms? (1 kg ≈ 2.2 lb)

items.q: Track A is 5 kilometers long. Track B is 5 miles long (1 km ≈ 0.6 mi). Which track is longer?

options.fb: 1 kilometer is only about 0.6 mile, so a kilometer is shorter than a mile.

options.t: Both tracks are the exact same length
options.fb: That's the Viper mistake! The numbers match, but miles and kilometers are different units.

options.t: You cannot tell without a calculator
options.fb: Knowing 1 km ≈ 0.6 mi tells you right away that 1 mile is longer than 1 kilometer.

items.q: Why do we write 1 mile ≈ 1.61 km with ≈ instead of =?

options.t: The conversion factor is rounded, so the result is approximate
Customary and metric units can never be compared
options.fb: They can be compared once converted; ≈ just shows the factor was rounded.

options.t: Miles and kilometers measure different things
options.fb: Both measure distance. The ≈ symbol means approximately equal.

options.t: You are supposed to guess the answer
options.fb: An approximation is a careful calculation with a rounded factor, not a guess.

gates.pass: BUZZ! Drift Crew takes Round 1 — unit size first, ≈ for rounded factors!

gates.title: Gate 2 · Scale the Ratio Table
gates.prompt: Use the conversion factor as a ratio and scale it up for the quiz board.
hints: Conceptual: write the conversion factor as a ratio (like 1 : 2.54) and multiply both parts by the same scale factor.
Procedural: multiply inches by 2.54 to get cm; multiply kilometers by 0.6 to get approximate miles.

steps: Practice: convert 4 inches to centimeters (1 in = 2.54 cm).
Multiply both parts of 1 : 2.54 by 4: 4 × 2.54 = 10.16 cm.
worked.q: Convert 20 kilometers to miles using 1 km ≈ 0.6 mi.

fb.msg: Multiplying by 10 shifts the decimal one place right: 2.54 × 10 = 25.4, not 254.
That added 10 + 2.54. Scale the ratio 1 : 2.54 by multiplying by 10.

gates.pass: 25.4 cm and about 30 miles! Lin's ratio table is unstoppable.

gates.title: Gate 3 · Check the Direction
gates.prompt: A rival crew converted 3 kilograms to 1.36 pounds using 1 kg ≈ 2.2 lb. Catch the error and fix it!
hints: Conceptual: a pound is smaller than a kilogram, so 3 kilograms must be MORE than 3 pounds, not less.
Procedural: multiply 3 kg by 2.2 lb per kg instead of dividing.

steps: Practice: convert 4 kg to pounds (1 kg ≈ 2.2 lb).
Pounds are smaller than kilograms, so multiply: 4 × 2.2 = 8.8 pounds.
worked.q: Convert 2 kg to pounds (1 kg ≈ 2.2 lb).

options.t: Pounds are smaller than kilograms, so the number should be bigger than 3, not smaller
Kilograms and pounds should always have the exact same number
options.fb: Different units give different numbers for the same weight.

options.t: You should add 2.2 to 3 instead of multiplying
options.fb: Unit conversions scale by multiplying or dividing, never adding.

options.t: It is actually reasonable because 1.36 is close to 2.2
options.fb: Since 1 kg ≈ 2.2 lb, 3 kg must be much more than 2.2 lb.

items.label: 3 kilograms ≈ ___ pounds (1 kg ≈ 2.2 lb)

fb.msg: 5.2 is 3 + 2.2. Multiply by the conversion factor 2.2.
That divided 3 by 2.2. Multiply 3 × 2.2 to get pounds.

items.fbDefault: Multiply 3 kilograms by 2.2 pounds per kilogram.

gates.pass: 6.6 pounds! The Vipers forgot to check unit-size direction!

gates.title: Boss Gate · Championship Round
gates.prompt: Three championship questions across customary and metric systems.
hints: Conceptual: put both measurements into the same unit before comparing them.
Procedural: multiply or divide by the given conversion factor, and check whether the new unit is larger or smaller.

steps: Practice: compare 20 lb and 10 kg using 1 lb ≈ 0.45 kg.
9 kg < 10 kg, so 10 kg is heavier.
worked.q: About how many kilograms is 40 pounds? (1 lb ≈ 0.45 kg)

items.label: Lock 1 · 100 km/h ≈ ___ mi/h (1 km ≈ 0.6 mi)
items.aria: 100 kilometers per hour in miles per hour

fb.msg: Miles are longer than kilometers, so the miles-per-hour number must be smaller than 100.

items.label: Lock 2 · A kart weighs 10 pounds. About how many kg? (1 lb ≈ 0.45 kg)

fb.msg: Multiplying 0.45 by 10 shifts the decimal one place right: 4.5, not 45.
Check the factor: 1 lb ≈ 0.45 kg, so 10 lb ≈ 10 × 0.45 kg.

items.q: Lock 3 · A bumper strip is 5 inches long. A gap is 12 centimeters wide (1 in = 2.54 cm). Will the strip fit?

options.t: No — 5 inches is 12.7 cm, which is wider than 12 cm
Yes — 5 is smaller than 12, so it fits easily
options.fb: You cannot compare 5 inches and 12 centimeters without converting to the same unit.
Centimeters are smaller than inches, so 5 inches must be MORE than 5 cm (5 × 2.54 = 12.7 cm).

options.t: No — 5 inches is 7.54 cm, which is too short

gates.pass: DING-DING-DING! 60 mi/h, 4.5 kg, and 12.7 cm > 12 cm! Pole position belongs to Drift Crew!

journal.heading: Lesson 3-7 — what the cup quiz taught us
rows: Compare unit sizes before computing. Same number with a bigger unit (5 miles vs 5 km) is always the larger amount.
Use = for exact definitions like 1 in = 2.54 cm. Use ≈ for rounded factors like 1 km ≈ 0.6 mi.
Write the conversion factor as a ratio (1 : 0.6) and multiply both parts by the same factor.
Going to a smaller unit gives a bigger number; going to a larger unit gives a smaller number.
journal.quote: "Five kilometers and five miles are only equal if you measure with your eyes closed." — Spark

teacher.suggested: Use during or after lesson 3-7 (Convert Measurements Between Systems). Covers customary-to-metric and metric-to-customary conversions, ratio tables, exact vs approximate (≈), and reasonableness checks.
